gloss: mid-year Taoist observance; origin of お中元

definitions.gloss: mid-year Taoist observance; origin of お中元
definitions.explanation: Originally one of three Taoist calendrical observances, held on the 15th day of the 7th lunar month as a day of repentance and offerings for the dead. In Japan the term was absorbed into Buddhist Obon practice and gave its name to お{中元|ちゅうげん}, the modern midsummer gift-giving custom.

examples.english: The custom of お中元, giving summer gifts, has its origin in the Taoist observance called chuugen.

notes:
{中元|ちゅうげん} was originally one of three Taoist calendrical observances ({三元|さんげん}: {上元|じょうげん}, {中元|ちゅうげん}, {下元|かげん}), each tied to a full moon of the lunar calendar. {中元|ちゅうげん} fell on the 15th day of the 7th lunar month and was a day of repentance, when offerings were made to ease the suffering of the dead.

CULTURAL NOTE:
When this observance reached Japan, it merged with the Buddhist {盂蘭盆|うらぼん} (Obon) tradition of honoring ancestors. The custom of giving gifts around this time of year evolved into today's お{中元|ちゅうげん}, the midsummer gift-giving custom for people one is grateful to.

The original religious meaning of {中元|ちゅうげん} is largely forgotten in modern Japan; most people encounter the word only as part of お{中元|ちゅうげん}.
